parameters.formDescription: Raise a purchase requisition. Pricing is derived from approved vendor catalogs.

nodes.name: Procurement Request Form
nodes.notes:
Entry point 1 of 2. Reliable structured path; feeds the baseline from day 1.
The business_unit dropdown is GENERATED from the business_units table. Adding a BU means re-running the generator, not editing this node.

nodes.name: Normalize Request
nodes.notes:
Every entry point converges here on ONE request object, so everything downstream sees one shape.
Mints request_id (deterministic on content + minute).
THROWS on an invalid quantity rather than defaulting. Inventing a value is a silent failure.

nodes.name: Vendor Catalog Lookup
nodes.notes:
READS: vendor_catalog, filtered on sku + category.
SKU-level ASL: the rows are the vendors approved to supply THIS item.
No rows = no approved source. Handled, not an error.

nodes.name: Best Price + Maverick Flag
nodes.notes:
The amount is DERIVED here, never asserted by the requester.
Ranks approved vendors by unit price, then applies the BU's max_lead_time_days: the cheapest source that can actually arrive in time wins.
If NOTHING meets tolerance: takes the fastest, sets lead_time_breach, forces a human.
Flags maverick when the requester named a vendor that is not the best source.

nodes.name: Catalog Match?
nodes.notes:
Priced -> ROUTE. No approved source -> sourcing event.
A no-match is never an auto-approve and never a silent drop.

assignments.name: stub_note
assignments.value: ROADMAP: three-quote collection. Detection ships in the pilot; the sourcing event itself is spec'd, not built.

nodes.name: Needs Sourcing (RFQ)
nodes.notes:
Terminal for this pilot. Detection ships; three-quote collection is ROADMAP.
Still writes a full event row and posts to #orders.

nodes.name: DoA Rule Lookup
nodes.notes:
READS: doa_rules, filtered on business_unit + category.
Returns every threshold band for that BU. No rows is a legitimate state and it becomes a default-deny downstream, never a pass.

nodes.name: Threshold Eval + Self-Check
nodes.notes:
Deterministic. No LLM on this path, so the golden set is a TEST SUITE, not model eval.
Selects the band by amount and reads approval_mode from the row: single vs dual is CONFIG, not code.
DEFAULT-DENY on: no rule row, lead-time breach, amount outside all bands, overlapping bands.
self_check asserts exactly one band claims the amount.

nodes.name: Route Decision
nodes.notes:
Four outputs: auto-approve / single / dual / DEFAULT-DENY.
Fallback output is default-deny by design. An unrecognised route must reach a human.

assignments.name: stub_note
assignments.value: Under the configured auto_approve_under ceiling. Still writes a full event trail.

nodes.name: Auto-Approved
nodes.notes:
Under the BU's configured auto_approve_under ceiling.
Still writes a full event trail and still posts an outcome. Auto does not mean invisible.

nodes.name: Build Event Row
nodes.notes: One row per state transition. This table IS the instrument.

nodes.name: Write Event Row
nodes.notes:
WRITES: pr_events.
Cycle time, stall rate, off-contract rate and rule drift are all queries against this table. A dashboard is roadmap; the table is the deliverable.

nodes.name: Procurement Mailbox (IMAP)
nodes.notes:
Entry point 2 of 2. Disabled until a mailbox credential is wired.
IMAP not Gmail: no public OAuth redirect on this box, and the customer is a connector swap anyway.

nodes.name: Parse Request Email
nodes.notes:
DETERMINISTIC parse, no LLM. At this company size the request mail is already a template, so it is a regex problem.
Handles label aliases and cuts quoted/forwarded history so a reply thread cannot inject a stale SKU.
Whether the mail is templated is a DISCOVERY finding, not an assumption.

nodes.name: Parse OK?
nodes.notes:
Requires business_unit + sku + a positive numeric quantity.
Anything short of that bounces. It never routes on a guess.

assignments.name: stub_note
assignments.value: Non-conforming mail. Reply with a prefilled form link rather than guessing. Cheap, and it cannot be wrong. LLM extraction is the roadmap item, justified only if the mailbox sample shows a tail big enough to matter.

nodes.name: Bounce Back (form link)
nodes.notes:
Reply with a prefilled form link. Cheap, and it cannot be wrong.
LLM extraction stays roadmap, justified only if the mailbox sample shows a non-conforming tail big enough to matter.

nodes.name: Notify #requests
nodes.notes: Side branch, NOT a pipeline stage. A notification must never sit between two steps that pass data, or the next step receives an HTTP response instead of the request.

nodes.name: Post to #requests
nodes.notes:
Webhook URL from the container env (fed from the secret store). Nothing secret is stored in this workflow, so an export leaks nothing.
Terminal branch.

nodes.name: Build Approval Card
nodes.notes:
Builds the Slack card and BOTH decision links from this execution's Wait resume URL.
n8n already signs that URL, so the links are joined with & (a second ? swallows the signature and the resume 401s).
Same link works from email: the approval is state-shaped, not Slack-shaped.

nodes.name: Post to #approvals
nodes.notes:
#approvals holds ONLY undecided items, so it stays a work queue. Outcomes go to #orders.
Webhook URL from container env.

nodes.name: Wait for Decision
nodes.notes:
Resumes on the decision link, or times out after the BU's escalation_hours.
A timeout carries NO decision, which IS the escalation signal.
State survives restarts because it is a row, not a variable in a running process.

nodes.name: Apply Decision
nodes.notes:
approve / reject / timeout -> escalate to approver_fallback.
The fallback approver comes from the rules table. Data, not a code change.

nodes.name: Build Outcome
nodes.notes:
Every terminal state posts an outcome: approved, rejected, escalated, no-match.
Posting only approvals is not an audit trail.
Computes time-to-decision, which is the number the 90-day review is built on.
Does NOT mint a PO number: the ERP owns that sequence, and a number that exists only here is a reconciliation problem handed to the customer.

nodes.name: Post to #orders
nodes.notes: Side branch, terminal. Webhook URL from container env.

nodes.name: Load BU Policy
nodes.notes:
Collapses the BU's rule rows into ONE item carrying the request + its policy.
NOT cosmetic: a Data Table lookup runs once per INPUT item, so letting 3 band rows through fans the catalog lookup out into 3 duplicate copies of every vendor.
Takes the STRICTEST max_lead_time_days if bands ever disagree.

parameters.content:
# FieldOps Co. - Procure-to-Approve  (pilot: BU-01, MRO)
**One workflow. The business units differ in their CONFIG ROWS, not in their shape.**

`INTAKE → POLICY → PRICE → ROUTE → APPROVE → RECORD`

Load the BU's policy, price within it, route on the derived amount, gate it with a human, record every transition.

Canvas = what this is and what each part's contract is. The maintainer doc = why it is shaped this way. Values live in neither: they are in the config tables.

## [1. INTAKE](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-intake)
**Two entry points, 1 pipeline.**

IN: a form submission or an email.
OUT: one normalized request object with a request_id.
READS: [business_units](https://your-runbook.example/#business_units-the-bu-registry) (for the dropdown).

**Form** is the reliable structured path and feeds the baseline from day 1.
**Email** using their current request pattern, parsed deterministically. Non-conforming mail bounces back with a form link.

ON FAILURE: an invalid quantity THROWS rather than defaulting to 1. Inventing a value is a silent failure that reaches a purchase order.

## [2. POLICY](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-policy)
**Load the BU's rules before pricing.**

IN: normalized request.
OUT: request + that BU's policy, as ONE item.
READS: [doa_rules](https://your-runbook.example/#doa_rules-the-policy-master) on business_unit + category.

Pricing has to happen INSIDE the policy, because the lead-time tolerance decides which vendors are even eligible.

ON FAILURE: no rule rows is legitimate (a BU can exist with no policy yet). It becomes an explicit default-deny in ROUTE, never a pass.

## [3. PRICE](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-price)
**The amount is DERIVED, never asserted.**

IN: request + policy.
OUT: best source, derived amount, savings vs incumbent, flags.
READS: [vendor_catalog](https://your-runbook.example/#vendor_catalog-the-approved-supplier-list) on sku + category (SKU-level ASL).

Ranks approved vendors by unit price, then applies the BU's `max_lead_time_days`. The cheapest vendor that can arrive in time is chosen; if a cheaper vendor is dropped for being too slow, the extra cost is recorded.

ON FAILURE:
• no approved source → sourcing event, never an auto-approve
• nothing inside tolerance → fastest available, flagged, forced to a human

## [4. ROUTE](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-route)
**The DoA matrix IS the routing engine.**

IN: priced request.
OUT: one of auto-approve / single / dual / default-deny.
READS: the policy already loaded in step 2.

Deterministic, and it grades its own output. 8 BUs differ in thresholds and approvers, not in shape: one workflow, N config rows.

**DEFAULT-DENY on:** missing rule row, lead-time breach, amount outside all bands, overlapping bands, unrecognised route.
A missing config row must NEVER auto-approve.

## [5. APPROVE](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-approve)
**One gate, three routes.**

IN: a routed request.
OUT: approved / rejected / escalated.
POSTS: #approvals (undecided items only, so it stays a work queue).

Single, dual and default-deny differ in their DATA (approver, mode, reason)
Slack buttons carry this execution's signed, single-use resume URL. The same link works from email.
ON FAILURE: a timeout carries no decision, which IS the escalation signal. The fallback approver comes from the rules table.

**After the gate, the outcome forks by state.** *Approved?* takes an approval to the order post and the ready-for-PO email. *Rejected?* fires the [Revision Loop](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-revision-loop).

**Reject is a loop, not a terminal state.** The Reject button opens a mandatory reason form, which resumes the request with `decision=reject` and the reason. The requester gets the reason plus a pre-filled link back into intake; the revised request is a NEW run, re-priced and re-routed from scratch, so a smaller order can now auto-approve. Capped at 3 attempts, then REJECTED_FINAL to requester + cost owner. Every pass links to the original request, so rework rate is a query.

## [6. RECORD + CLOSE](https://your-runbook.example/#zone-record)
**The instrument is a table, not a dashboard.**

IN: any terminal state.
OUT: one row per request at its terminal state, plus an outcome post.
WRITES: [pr_events](https://your-runbook.example/#pr_events-the-audit-log).  POSTS: #orders.

Cycle time, stall rate, off-contract rate, rework rate and rule drift are all queries against this table. A dashboard is roadmap.

Every terminal state posts, including rejections and escalations. Posting only approvals is not an audit trail.

The row carries `revision_of` and `revision_count`, so a rejection that returns as a revision stays one linked chain, and rework is queryable.

**No PO number is invented here.** The ERP owns that sequence.

## [RUNBOOK - onboard a business unit](https://your-runbook.example/#onboard-a-business-unit)
*You should not need to open a single node to do this.*

**1.** Add the BU to the **[business_units](https://your-runbook.example/#business_units-the-bu-registry)** table (`code`, `name`, `active`).

**2.** Add its rows to **[doa_rules](https://your-runbook.example/#doa_rules-the-policy-master)**, one per threshold band:
`business_unit, category, threshold_min, threshold_max, approver_primary, approver_fallback, approval_mode, escalation_hours, auto_approve_under, max_lead_time_days, cost_center`

**3.** Run the golden set. If it passes, that BU is live.

Bands must not overlap: the evaluator asserts exactly one band claims an amount and default-denies if more than one does.

A BU with no rows is safe. Every request from it default-denies to a human until somebody writes the policy. That is deliberate.

## [CONFIGURATION](https://your-runbook.example/#config-tables-change-these-not-the-canvas)
*Four tables. Everything that changes weekly is in one of them, and none of it is on this canvas.*

**[doa_rules](https://your-runbook.example/#doa_rules-the-policy-master)** - thresholds, approvers, escalation windows, approval mode, lead-time tolerance. The routing engine.

**[vendor_catalog](https://your-runbook.example/#vendor_catalog-the-approved-supplier-list)** - the hosted vendor catalogs. SKU-level ASL: which vendors are approved for which item, at what price and lead time.

**[business_units](https://your-runbook.example/#business_units-the-bu-registry)** - the BU master. Separate from the rules on purpose: a BU can exist before anyone has written its policy.

**[pr_events](https://your-runbook.example/#pr_events-the-audit-log)** - every state transition. Read-only in practice; this is the measurement instrument.

Changing an approver or a threshold is a ROW EDIT, not a deploy. Nobody has to open n8n.

## [TROUBLESHOOTING](https://your-runbook.example/#troubleshooting)

**Everything from one BU is denying.** It has no rows in [doa_rules](https://your-runbook.example/#doa_rules-the-policy-master), or its bands overlap. Check `route_reason` on the event row.

**A request took an unexpected vendor.** Check `max_lead_time_days` for that BU: the cheapest source may not meet its tolerance. `lead_time_premium` shows what the tolerance cost.

**An approval link says invalid token.** Resume URLs are single-use and die once actioned. Expected behaviour, not a fault.

**Nothing arrived in Slack.** The webhook URLs come from the container env. Check they are present before suspecting the workflow.

**It is 2am and it is broken.** Find the request_id in [pr_events](https://your-runbook.example/#pr_events-the-audit-log), read the last transition, and the failure is in the next step. Nothing is lost, because state is a row and not a variable in a running process.

## [FAILURE MODES](https://your-runbook.example/#failure-modes)
*The failure mode this workflow is built to refuse.*

A run can be green and still be wrong. Four places that is defended:

**1.** A missing rule row default-denies instead of passing.
**2.** A low-confidence email parse bounces instead of routing.
**3.** The threshold evaluator grades its own output (`self_check`).
**4.** An unmeetable lead time is flagged, not quietly ignored.

**The weekly query that matters:** requests that entered and never terminated. n8n will show you green executions. Green is not the same as done.

The golden set is the artifact that keeps this true after a config change. Run it after every rule edit.
